data.title: Active
data.tagline: Show that a control is being pressed right now
data.description: The active state appears during the press between pointer down and release. A small change in color, depth, or scale confirms that the input was received. It is different from a selected item that stays chosen after the interaction.

use: Give a button press physical feedback
Show a menu item while it is being clicked
Respond to a pointer or key press
avoid: Use active styling as the permanent selected state
Scale a control so far that the layout jumps
Remove all feedback during a press
Make the pressed state look disabled

lessonPractice.title: A submit button shows no change between pointer down and release, so users often click twice. What feedback should be added?

options.label: Change color or position slightly while pressed, restore on release, and support keyboard activation
options.feedback: A brief change responds directly to input and restores before it can be mistaken for selection or disablement.

options.label: Keep the pressed style after the first click until the user clicks again
options.feedback: Persistent styling expresses a toggle or selection rather than the moment from press to release.

options.label: Keep only the hover color and add no press-to-release feedback because hover already shows it is clickable
options.feedback: Hover only shows where the pointer is; it does not confirm a press and may not appear during keyboard activation.

data.agentPrompt: Add a brief pressed state to the submit button: darken or lower it slightly during pointer or keyboard press, then restore on release, leave, or cancel. Do not turn it into persistent selection or shift surrounding layout.
